Exercise A

too and enough

Use too before an adjective (too small), enough after an adjective (big enough) and before a noun (enough time). Choose the correct form for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Twelve things that are too much or not enough

1. The flat is 1 small for four people.

2. The room is not big 2 for a desk and a bed.

3. I don’t have 3 time to finish the course this term.

4. It is 4 cold to study in the library without a jacket.

5. There are 5 many people on the bus, so we can’t sit down.

6. This app is 6 to use, so even beginners can try it.

7. She is 7 to live alone yet.

8. The rent is too high 8 me to pay.

9. There is 9 noise at night, so I can’t sleep.

10. Are there 10 chairs for everyone in the room?

11. Out of all the courses I have taken, this is the 11 (interesting).

12. By the time we arrived, the agent 12 (leave).

Exercise B

Write a recommendation

Plan for 5 minutes, then write alone for 15 minutes. Imagine a new student asks you for advice. Your teacher reads your text.

Word count: 0

Write 80–110 words. Say what you recommend, give two reasons with comparatives, and mention one thing that is too… or not … enough. Finish with I would recommend… or I would not recommend….

Exercise C

Check a partner’s text

Swap texts with a partner in the chat. Read your partner’s recommendation and write one useful tip.

Find one comparative and one too / enough phrase in your partner’s text. Then write one tip: something to add, or one thing to fix.
